source_text: Instituens quippe Deus, quae in examinibus deberet forma servari, praescripsit ne innocentia necessitudinis suae periculis iungeretur, atque ut patrem a supplicio peccantis filii, ita filium a patris condemnatione separavit, ostendens profecto simili exitu utriusque personae tam non posse parentum ad filios peccata transire, quam nec filiorum transeunt ad parentes.
pass_a_gloss: For God, instituting what form ought to be kept in examinations, prescribed that innocence not be joined to the dangers of its kinship, and as he separated the father from the punishment of a sinning son, so the son from the father's condemnation, showing surely by a like outcome of each person that parents' sins can no more pass to sons than sons' sins pass to parents.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: In establishing the pattern to be followed in trials, God commanded that innocence should not be implicated in the dangers faced by a relative. Just as he separated the father from the punishment of a sinful son, he separated the son from the father’s condemnation. By giving both persons the same outcome, he clearly showed that parents’ sins can no more pass to children than children’s sins pass to parents.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Continues the explicit argument from the law forbidding punishment of parents and children for one another’s sins.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
